add_to_this_grid: A new cube on the same grid as the form being edited, set down beside what is there. Forms on one grid are kept clear of each other and turn together. Choose another kind from Form, or drag the cube's dots to make it a floor or a wall.
arch_askew: This arch runs at an angle to the brick grid: its feet differ along both X and Y. No flat outline can be fitted to it, so it is fitted cell by cell and comes out stepped.
arch_kind: The shape of the arch between its two feet.
bezier_pull: How strongly this point draws the curve towards itself. 1 is neutral.
blend: How far the join between this form and the forms it stands in is rounded, in microbricks along each of them. At 0 the two meet in a sharp crease. The bricks are fitted afresh where the forms meet and are each form's own everywhere else. A form is joined by moving it into another with Ctrl held.
brick_budget: The smallest brick size that keeps the build within this many bricks is used. A form laid as a pattern of tiles is not held to it, and nor is a plant: both are built at single microbricks unless you set a Brick size.
brick_size: Fits the form with bricks a multiple of this size. Automatic picks the finest size that keeps the build within the brick budget.
claude_command: Run this once in a terminal to tell Claude Code where the editor is. After that, start Claude Code, tick the box above, and ask it to build something.
claude_on: Lets Claude add, change, colour, turn and remove forms in this workspace while you watch, through the Model Context Protocol. Off until you tick it, and off again each time the program starts. While it is on, the editor listens on this computer only; every change Claude makes is named at the top of the view and can be taken back with Ctrl+Z.
clear_reports: Deletes every saved report file. Nothing else is touched.
closed_loop: Joins the last point back to the first.
colour_mode: How the form is coloured: one colour, a blend from one colour to another, stripes, or as its pattern has it. Each brick is one colour.
colour_runs_along: The direction a blend or stripes run in across the form.
colours: The colours used. Click one to change it. A blend or stripes take up to four and a pattern up to eight, added with + and taken away with -. Right-click a colour to copy it, and right-click another to paste it there.
copy_to_clipboard: Writes the form being edited, and any others marked +, to brickloft-build.brz, a Brickadia prefab file, and puts that file on the clipboard. Ctrl+C does the same, and Ctrl+V adds the forms of a copied file back to the workspace.
cube_size: How long the cube is along this axis, in whole microbricks. Its middle stays where it is. To move one side alone, drag the dot on it. A pattern is laid through the shortest of the three lengths, so it shows on the largest face.
depth: How deep a flat band is, measured across the plane its curve lies in.
discrepancy: The volume where the bricks and the true form disagree: missing material plus extra material.
dots_move: Which way a dragged dot moves: in the plane facing the camera, or with one of its coordinates kept as it is.
duplicate_form: A copy of the form being edited on the same grid, coloured the same, set down beside it. Ctrl+D does the same.
facing: The axis the circle faces along. Z lays it flat.
fill_curve: Fills everything the curve encloses: a ring becomes a disc, an arch a filled arch.
flip: Mirror the finished form along an axis, about the middle of its points.
floor_below_form: Lowers the floor in the view so you can look at a form from underneath. The floor is also see-through from below. It changes nothing that is built.
form: The kind of form to build. Choosing one starts it at its usual size.
go_to_folder: Opens this folder of saved forms in your file manager. Each save there is a .brz prefab file that the game can load as it stands.
grass_action: What a touch of the brush does to the ground under the grass. Push up raises a hill. Push down lowers the ground, below the level the patch lies on if you go on: a hollow deeper than the water stands fills with water. Flatten brings the ground to the height it has where you touch it.
grass_intensity: How far a push raises or lowers the ground at the middle of the brush, in microbricks. Dragging a touch's dot up or down changes it too.
grass_level: The height a flattening touch brings the ground to, in microbricks over the floor.
grass_passable: Ticked, the blades of grass are written with their collision off, so that a player in the game walks through them and stands on the soil underneath. Unticked, the blades are as solid as any brick.
grass_range: How far the brush reaches from where it touches. A wide brush makes a broad hill or hollow that runs smoothly into the ground round it.
grid_at_an_angle: Bricks sit on a grid, and a grid other than the world's can stand at any angle. This grid has been turned by its rings, so everything on it is copied to the clipboard on a grid of its own. Grids pass through each other, so it is in no other grid's way.
line_up: Gives the arch a grid of its own, turned so that the arch runs straight along it, with its feet left where they are. Bricks on a grid at an angle are fitted as if it were level, so the arch comes out as smooth as any other. Ctrl+Z takes it back.
longest_brick: The longest edge a single brick may have, in microbricks. 80 is what the game was seen to accept when this was first tried; the game's own limit is said to be 800 studs, which is 4000 microbricks. Raise it and paste to find out: a form then needs fewer, longer bricks.
maze_divisions: How many cells the first ring round the room is cut into by spokes. Fewer are used if that many would not leave room to pass between them.
maze_entrance: Where on the rim the way in is, in degrees round from the X axis. The cell of the outermost ring at that angle is opened to the outside.
maze_floor: A floor under the whole maze, this many microbricks thick, out to the outside of its rim. The walls stand on it. It is the first of the maze's colours.
maze_gap: From the middle of one ring wall to the middle of the next: a corridor and one wall. Changing it keeps the number of rings and resizes the maze. The dot on the rim does the same by dragging. A corridor is never less than 3 microbricks between its walls.
maze_grow: How the number of cells in a ring grows outwards. Left to keep cells square, a ring has twice the cells of the ring inside it wherever its cells would otherwise be more than twice as wide as the corridor. Otherwise it doubles every so many rings, as long as there is room to pass between the spokes. It only ever doubles, so every spoke of a ring lines up with a spoke of the ring outside it.
maze_height: How tall the walls stand above the floor. The dot over the middle of the maze does the same by dragging. A hedge is never under 12.
maze_kind: Which maze. Theta is rings of corridors about a round room, with walls that are arcs and spokes. Grid is square cells about a square room. Either has one way in, on its rim, and one way to the room in the middle; every part of it can be reached, and there are no loops.
maze_rings: How many rings the maze has, the room in the middle counted as the first. Changing it keeps the corridors as wide as they are, so the maze grows or shrinks. A grid has this many cells from its middle to its edge.
maze_seed: Which maze: any whole number, each a different one. Another takes the next number. The same number and settings are always the same maze.
maze_solution: Lays a strip one microbrick high along the ground from the way in to the room in the middle, in a colour of its own: the last of the maze's colours, or the third if its walls are plain. Untick it before copying a maze that is meant to be solved.
maze_texture: What the walls are made of. None is plain walls in one colour. Hedge grows the Plant form's hedge along every wall, with its own density, looseness and berries; it is at least 6 thick and 12 tall, and is tens of thousands of bricks. Planks, bricks, cobblestone and medallions are wrapped along each wall: courses of bricks run level along a wall and bend round the rings with it. A texture colours the walls and never moves them, so the long sloped bricks of a curved face are each one colour to a course. Choosing a texture brings its colours unless you have set your own: the first is the floor and the mortar, the last the strip that marks the way through.
mirror: Make the form its own mirror image along an axis: its low side along that axis is kept, and the high side becomes its mirror image, about the middle of the form's dots. An arch with one foot higher than the other gets two feet alike; a point added to one side of a circle appears on the other too.
natural_height: Ticked, the arch takes the height its shape gives it: a round arch is a semicircle. Dragging the top dot sets your own height.
neighbouring_dots_follow: How much of a dragged dot's movement the dots near it share: 0 moves it alone, 1 takes its nearest neighbours almost all the way with it. The share falls away with distance, out to three times the reach of added points.
new_grid: A new cube on a grid of its own, which its rings turn to any angle and its arrows move, apart from every other grid.
pattern: A texture to lay the form as, in place of plain brick. Stepping stones are separate stones of any shape, or with the gap at 0 stones fitted together. Medallions repeats a few ringed figures over the whole floor. Rug is a Persian carpet: nested borders, a lobed medallion with pendants, corner pieces, and scrolling stems with flowers and leaves. Planks is a floor of boards. Bricks is courses of bricks, every one a rectangle. Cobblestone is stones of any shape fitted together. Both can be as uneven as you ask, with or without mortar. Stepping stones need a flat form. The others colour the form without reshaping it: they are laid through a flat form, on the flat part of a form that is not flat all over, and on the sides of a box. Choosing a pattern brings its colours with it unless you have set your own: the first colour is the ground or the mortar, and the others are shared among the pattern's parts, up to eight.
pattern_bevel: Slopes the top microbrick of every brick down to its edge, all round it, with the mortar at the foot of the slope. It needs the form to be 2 or more deep, and is cut into one face: the top of a floor.
pattern_border: How many microbricks of plain ground are left round the edge of the pattern.
pattern_mortar: Whether there is a microbrick of mortar between one piece and the next. Without it they touch, and are told apart by their shades alone, so give the pattern several colours.
pattern_seed: Which one of the pattern: any whole number, each a different one. Another takes the next number and the next of the pattern's sets of colours.
pattern_size: How large the boards, bricks or cobbles are. 2 is the usual size, 1 half of it and 4 twice.
pattern_stagger: How far each course is moved along from the one before, as a share of a brick's length. 50% is the usual half-brick bond, 0% stacks the bricks in columns, and 25% or 33% make the joints step across the wall.
pattern_stagger_uneven: Moves each course along by an amount of its own, so that the upright joints fall anywhere. Untick it to set one stagger for every course.
pattern_uneven_across: How unlike one another the pieces are across the courses. For bricks it moves the lines between courses, so that the courses differ in depth. For cobbles it moves each stone's point up and down.
pattern_uneven_along: How unlike one another the pieces are along the courses. For bricks it moves the joints, so that the bricks differ in length and stay rectangles. For cobbles it moves each stone's point from side to side.
pattern_upright: Runs the courses up the floor instead of across it, so that the bricks stand on end and the stagger is from side to side.
pyramid_height: The pyramid's height. Left alone it is as tall as half its base is wide.
quarter_turn: Turn the form a quarter turn about an axis, within the brick grid. The form is the same bricks whichever way it faces. For any other angle, drag one of the red, green or blue rings round: that turns the form's whole grid.
radius: The form's size from its middle to its edge, in microbricks. Ctrl + scroll over the view changes it too.
ramps_and_corners: Unticked, the form is built of cubes alone, as a staircase.
reach_of_added_points: How far from each added point the form goes with it: along a curve to either side, or all round on a sphere or pyramid.
remove_form: Take the form being edited out of the workspace.
reset_form: Put the dots, sizes, stretch, flips and other choices back to how this form starts out. How it is fitted and coloured is left alone.
round_tube: Builds the curve as a round tube, which for a circle is a torus. Unticked it is a flat band with a thickness and a depth.
save_report: Writes out this form's settings, its bricks, and a cell-by-cell comparison of the bricks with the form: where material is missing or extra. Useful for working out why a fit looks wrong. Reports go in the folder brickloft in the system's temporary folder. If the editor ever closes by itself, brickloft-crash.txt in that folder says why.
save_screenshot: Saves a picture of the window in Pictures/brickloft and puts it on the clipboard. F12 does the same, and Shift+F12 leaves this panel out of the picture.
saved_add: Add its forms to the workspace, beside the form being edited and on its grid.
saved_delete: Delete this saved form. You are asked first.
saved_drag: Drag onto the view to add it to the workspace.
saved_folder: The folder of saved forms shown below. Add folder makes a new one.
saved_forms: A save holds the whole workspace: every form, with its colours and the grid it is on.
saved_open: Open in place of everything in the workspace. Ctrl+Z brings the workspace back.
saved_save: Saves the whole workspace under this name in the chosen folder: every form, with its colours and the grid it is on. A save of the same name is replaced.
segment_from: Where the segment starts, measured up from the sphere's centre.
segment_to: Where the segment ends, measured up from the sphere's centre.
show_parts: What is drawn over the bricks, each switched on its own. Rulers give the form's size along each axis in microbricks. Rings turn the form's grid to any angle. Arrows move the form being edited, and any picked with it, along one axis. Dots are the form's own points and sizes, which you drag to reshape it. Anything hidden cannot be taken hold of either, so it is never in the way.
simplify: How much closer a ramp must bring the outline to be worth a brick, in microbricks of area. 0 is the closest fit whatever the count; higher gives fewer, longer pieces. Flat forms only: on a 3D form, use Brick size.
sliders_go_up_to: How far every size slider reaches, in microbricks: radius, height, thickness, depth and the reach of added points. Lower it for a finer slider. Large forms take longer to fit.
snap_after_every_drag: Runs Snap to best fit nearby by itself each time a drag ends.
snap_best_fit: A form fits cleanly only where its surfaces land on the brick grid. This tries each dot and size up to a microbrick either way and keeps whatever fits closest.
snap_half_microbricks: Dots snap to half microbricks, which are single game units. Unticked they snap to whole microbricks.
solid_cube: Solid all through, or hollow with walls as thick as Wall thickness on every side. A hollow box too short to have a hollow inside is open through its shortest length: a frame.
solid_pyramid: Solid all through, or a hollow tent open underneath.
solid_revolve: Solid all through, or a shell along the profile as thick as Wall thickness: a vase or a bowl.
solid_sphere: Solid all through, or a hollow shell as thick as Wall thickness.
sphere_keep: The whole sphere, a dome (its top half), or a segment between two heights.
stone_gap: How wide the gap between neighbouring stones is, in microbricks. At 0 the stones are fitted together with no gap, as in a stone wall or a paved floor.
stone_size: About how far apart the middles of neighbouring stones are, in microbricks. A stone is a little under this across.
stone_uneven: 0 gives stones as alike in size as scattered stones can be. 1 gives some crowded small and others left large.
stretch: Stretches the form along this axis: 2 makes it twice as long that way, 0.5 half as long.
stretch_circle: Stretches the circle along this axis into an ellipse: 2 makes it twice as long that way, 0.5 half as long. How thick a ring or a round tube is, is its Thickness.
stripe_width: How wide each stripe is, in microbricks.
thickness: How thick the band, the tube or the wall is, in microbricks.
tree_bend: A pine: how far its boughs droop. A palm: how far its trunk leans. An oak or beech: how crooked its limbs are. A boxwood, hedge or hydrangea: how uneven its outline, from freshly clipped to grown out. A peony: how open its bloom is, from a round bud to full blown. A sunflower: how far its head nods. A tulip: how open its cup. Petunias: how far they trail from the mound. Reeds: how far they lean and their leaves flop. A birch, willow or Scots pine: how crooked its limbs. A cypress: how uneven its outline. A yucca: how far its blades bend over. A bed: how unevenly its flowers stand.
tree_colours: A set of colours for the plant's parts: bark or stem, three greens, limbs, and its petals, blooms or extras. Pines have a set under snow, oaks have autumn sets, and peonies and tulips come in several colours. Change any colour below to make a set of your own.
tree_count: A pine: how many tiers of boughs. A palm: how many fronds in its crown. An oak: how many limbs its trunk divides into. A beech: how many limbs leave its trunk. A boxwood: how many stems. A hedge: how many plants stand along it. A peony, sunflower or tulip: how many flowers stand in the clump, each a different height. A hydrangea: how many flower heads. Petunias: how many flowers. Reeds: how many stems. A birch, willow or Scots pine: its main limbs. A date palm: its fronds. A yucca: its blades. Daisies, daffodils or a bed: how many flowers. Grass: how far below the lawn water stands in a hollow, in microbricks; 0 for no water.
tree_extras: A pine: a star on top and baubles under the boughs. A palm: a cluster of coconuts under the crown. A boxwood or hedge: berries, in the seventh colour. An oak or beech: bare, with twigs where its leaves were. Reeds: the feathery plumes of common reed in place of a bulrush's brown heads. A birch, willow or Scots pine: bare. A date palm: bunches of dates. A yucca: its tall stalk of cream bells.
tree_fullness: A pine: how many boughs and how wide their sprays. A palm: how long its leaflets. An oak or beech: how large its masses of leaves, with less sky between them. A boxwood or hedge: how thick its canopy. A peony: how many petals and leaves. A sunflower: how large its petals and leaves. A tulip: how large its leaves. A hydrangea, petunias or reeds: how leafy.
tree_height: How tall the plant is, in microbricks. The dot at its top sets it too. Its twigs and petals are a microbrick or two thick at any size, so a tall plant has more detail than a short one.
tree_kind: Which plant. Trees: a pine (a spruce, the Christmas tree), a Scots pine, a coconut palm, a date palm, an oak, a beech, a birch, a weeping willow. Bushes: a boxwood, a hedge of it, a hydrangea, a cypress, a yucca. Flowers: a peony, sunflowers, tulips, petunias, daisies, daffodils, a bed of mixed flowers. And reeds and grass. Each is grown its own way. Choosing one starts it at its usual size and in its own colours.
tree_seed: Which plant of its kind: any whole number, each a different one. Another takes the next number. The same number is always the same plant.
tree_spread: How far the plant reaches to each side: a pine's longest boughs, a palm's fronds, an oak's crown, a bush's width. For a flower it is half the width of its head or cup, and a clump is wider. The dot at its side sets it too.
tube_protruded: Flat bands side by side, each standing proud of the next.
tube_rounded: A pipe: the edges chamfered round with sloped pieces.
tube_section: How a round tube's section is made. Rounded is a pipe with chamfered edges. Protruded is flat bands of different widths side by side: smooth along the curve and stepped across it.
whole_circle: Builds the whole circle through the three points, where unticked it is the arc from the first point to the last.
workspace: Forms stand on grids. Forms on one grid are kept clear of each other and are turned together by the rings. The arrows move the form being edited and any picked with it (Shift + click), and the whole grid when all of it is picked. Hold Ctrl while dragging a form to move it into another instead: the two are then one build, fitted afresh where they meet. Grids pass through each other.
workspace_buttons: Add to this grid sets a new cube beside the forms on this grid: they are kept clear of each other and turn together. New grid gives the new cube a grid of its own, which its rings turn to any angle. Duplicate adds a copy of the form being edited to its grid, in the same colours. Remove takes the form being edited out of the workspace.
workspace_form: Edit this form, and its grid. Clicking it in the view does the same.
sharp_corners: Ticked, the hedge, reeds or grass runs straight from dot to dot and turns a corner at each. Unticked, it follows a smooth curve through them.
grass_reeds: How thickly reeds stand in the shallows and on the bank of a pond, from none to many. A pond is any hollow pushed down deeper than the water stands.
grass_frozen: Ticked, the pond's water is written as ice: the same bricks with their collision on, so a player stands on it, and less see-through. Choosing the Winter colours ticks it and choosing any other set unticks it.
leaves_passable: Ticked, the plant's greenery (leaves, needles, fronds, petals, berries, baubles) is written with its collision off, so a player walks through the crown, and its wood (trunk, limbs, stems) stays solid. Unticked, all of it is solid.
